title: Cohort Groomer and Fallback Telemetry for Staged Model Admissions
creator: Maya Chen
description: We need a resilient subsystem that prepares (grooms) traffic cohorts for staged model admission, runs shadow probes, and drives automatic fallback/rollback decisions using telemetry. This ticket implements a Cohort Groomer service plus a Fallback Telemetry policy that the rollout engine can consult. Goals: 1) produce deterministic cohort slices to run A/B and canary variants against stable population definitions, 2) provide a low-latency signal path for short-window SLO checks (latency, errors, model-quality regressions), 3) support shadow probing (percent-based shadowing without affecting billing customers), and 4) define explicit, auditable rollback decisions for the rollout controller. Scope excludes the UI rollout editor (tracked in PM) but includes the API contract, simulation harness, and dashboard metrics needed for initial GA.
acceptance_criteria: Cohort Groomer API: create/list/get cohorts with deterministic hashing and sample seeds documented
Policy DSL: express step schedules with hold windows, metric guards, and soft/ hard thresholds
Shadow Probing: runtime supports atomically sending shadow copies to variant backends at configurable percentages without modifying customer response paths
Fallback Telemetry: latency/error/quality rules evaluate within 30s windows and return a stable decision to the rollout engine
Automated Rollback: rollout engine receives a clear 'rollback' decision and re-routes traffic within the SLA (<= 60s for traffic split change under load)
Simulations: test harness can run synthetic traffic and reproduce rollback scenarios deterministically
Documentation: API spec, example DSL snippets, and runbook for on-call engineers

example_policy_dsl:
stages:
  - name: shadow-probe
    action: shadow
    percent: 5
    hold_for: 10m
    guards:
      - metric: p95_latency_ms
        threshold: 1200
        operator: lt
      - metric: error_rate
        threshold: 0.003
        operator: lt
  - name: limited-exposure
    action: split
    percent: 20
    hold_for: 60m
    guards:
      - metric: p95_latency_ms
        threshold: 1000
        operator: lt
      - metric: quality_regression
        threshold: 0.02
        operator: lt
    on_violation:
      - backoff: exponential
      - notify: oncall@redwood.ai
  - name: ramp-to-prod
    action: split
    percent: 100
    hold_for: 24h
    guards:
      - metric: error_rate
        threshold: 0.0015
        operator: lt
notes_on_design: Cohort grooming uses keyed hashing on a stable user identifier (customer_id or device_fingerprint) plus an optional seed per rollout to provide reproducible slices. The Groomer returns cohort_ids and a sampling map that the runtime uses to route or shadow traffic. The Fallback Telemetry service subscribes to short-window metrics and evaluates guards compiled from the DSL. Decisions are emitted with an audit trail so rollouts are auditable and reversible. For model-quality guards we rely on sampled ground-truth callbacks (async scoring) and offline evals to seed expected distributions.
risks_mitigation: Risk: shadow copies could leak PII to downstream variants. Mitigation: enforce data-filtering middleware and add security review; shadow copies sanitized via KMS tokenization.
Risk: false-positive rollback from infra noise. Mitigation: require multi-metric violations plus temporal smoothing and population-level checks before triggering hard rollback.
Risk: cohort drift over time. Mitigation: log cohort assignment histograms and auto-detect significant drift; provide automated cohort rebalancing recommendations.
